ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A grain depot uses an electric motor with a rated voltage of U = 380 \mathrm{V} and an internal resistance of R = 0.25 \Omega to transport grain. The counterweight and the cable connecting the motor to the trolley are parallel to the inclined plane. The trolley loaded with grain moves uniformly uphill along the inclined plane at a speed of v = 2 \mathrm{m/s}, with a current of I = 40 \mathrm{A}. After the motor is turned off, the trolley continues to move uphill a distance L, reaching the unloading point, at which time its velocity becomes zero. After unloading the grain, giving the trolley an initial downward velocity allows it to move uniformly downhill along the inclined plane. Given the mass of the trolley m_1 = 100 \mathrm{kg}, the mass of the grain m_2 = 1200 \mathrm{kg}, the mass of the counterweight m_0 = 40 \mathrm{kg}, and the acceleration due to gravity g = 10 \mathrm{m/s^2}, the frictional force experienced by the trolley during movement is proportional to the total weight of the trolley and the grain, with a proportionality constant of k. The counterweight remains off the ground throughout the process, and the mechanical friction loss of the motor itself and the mass of the cable are negligible.

1. Determine the value of the proportionality constant k.
2. Request the value of the uphill distance L.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a cart located on an inclined track, and the track rises toward the upper right. The cart is connected with a rope along the direction of the inclined plane; there is a fixed pulley at the upper right, and beside it hangs a counterweight labeled Counterweight. The direction of action of the counterweight rope is transformed through the pulley and then acts on the cart along the direction of the inclined plane. At the lower right is a motor labeled Motor, and the motor also pulls the cart along the direction of the inclined plane through a rope. Therefore, the image shows that the actions of both the motor rope and the counterweight rope on the cart are parallel to the inclined plane; when the cart goes uphill, the counterweight provides an assisting pulling force upward along the inclined plane, and when the cart goes downhill, it hinders its sliding down. Reasoning: The useful mechanical power of the motor when the grain-loaded cart moves uphill at a uniform speed is the electric power minus the internal-resistance heat loss: P = UI - I^2R = 380×40 - 40^2×0.25 = 15200 - 400 = 14800 W. The cart speed v = 2 m/s, so the traction force of the motor on the cart is F = P/v = 14800/2 = 7400 N. Let the total mass when loaded with grain be M = m1 + m2 = 100 + 1200 = 1300 kg. After unloading the grain, the empty cart can move uniformly downward along the inclined plane with an initial speed. At this time, the gravitational component downward along the inclined plane equals the sum of the upward counterweight tension and friction force: m1 g sinθ = m0 g + k m1 g. Substituting m1 = 100 kg and m0 = 40 kg gives sinθ = 0.4 + k. When the grain-loaded cart moves uphill at a uniform speed, the motor traction force and counterweight tension upward along the inclined plane balance the gravitational component and friction force downward along the inclined plane: F + m0 g = M g sinθ + k M g. Substituting values: 7400 + 40×10 = 1300×10×(sinθ + k). That is, 7800 = 13000(sinθ + k). Substituting sinθ = 0.4 + k again gives 7800 = 13000(0.4 + 2k) = 5200 + 26000k, so k = 2600/26000 = 0.1. Thus sinθ = 0.5. After the motor is turned off, the grain-loaded cart continues uphill for distance L and then its speed becomes zero. Treat the grain-loaded cart and the counterweight as a whole; the initial kinetic energy is (1/2)(M + m0)v^2 = (1/2)×(1300 + 40)×2^2 = 2680 J. During the uphill process, the grain-loaded cart does work against the gravitational component and friction force, while the counterweight descends and its gravity does positive work, so the equivalent resistance consuming kinetic energy is M g(sinθ + k) - m0 g = 1300×10×(0.5 + 0.1) - 40×10 = 7800 - 400 = 7400 N. From the energy relation: 2680 = 7400L, giving L = 2680/7400 = 67/185 m.
